_doc: Hand-curated free-to-watch picks for the homepage panel. Edit this file to update the picks. Each entry: filmId from data/films.json + a one-line blurb. Build picks the canonical Verified+FREE link from the film's watchLinks; if no such link exists at build time the entry is skipped (with a warning).

picks.blurb: The Monkey King epic that proved Chinese animation could rival Disney — and shaped a generation of Asian animators.
Voted the greatest animated film of all time by 140 animators in 2003. Cutout. Mist. A bear with tea.
Norman McLaren's anti-war pixilation classic — won the Best Documentary Oscar even though it wasn't one.
Švankmajer's three-part stop-motion meditation on what conversation actually is. Direct line from here to the Brothers Quay.
Zagreb School cutout adaptation of Poe — proof Yugoslav animation could match anything coming out of Hollywood.
The first animated short ever made in Thailand. Hand-drawn by one man, Payut Ngaokrachang, in 1955.
Egypt, 1936 — the earliest surviving Arabic animated short, made in Cairo as Disney was still finding its feet.
Indian National Award winner that taught a generation of children about unity. Twelve minutes every '80s Indian schoolkid remembers by heart.
Juan Padrón's anti-imperial vampire comedy — sequel to Cuba's most internationally screened animated feature.
Norshteyn's other masterpiece. A wolf, a child, the smell of wet leaves, the inside of memory.
